note: Verdicts for upstream commits touching packages this fork deleted. Regenerate with `bun scripts/check-upstream-v2-delta.mjs --update`; see scripts/check-upstream-v2-delta.mjs for the gate itself. `tracked` = accepted debt recorded in packages/kimi-agent/ROADMAP.md §6; `not-applicable` = internal refactor with no observable engine behavior to port.

entries.subject: feat: turn filesystem watch back on by default (#4015)
entries.note: A two-line default flip in v2 (`human/utils/watch.ts` `watchEnabledFromConfig = false -> true`, `app/config/configService.ts` `?? false -> ?? true`), but the thing being flipped does not exist here: no `KIMI_CODE_WATCH`, no `setWatchEnabled`, no `[watch]` section in `packages/node-sdk/src/config-local/schema.ts`, and no watcher crate in `packages/kimi-agent/src` (no notify / inotify / ReadDirectoryChangesW). Measured port size: `watch.ts` is 756 lines exporting a whole `WatchService` + `NativeFsWatcher` runtime abstraction, with 12 production consumers (configService, fileWorkspacePersistence, app/watch/configSection, both skill sources, sessionInstructions, workspaceDirs, workspaceAgentProfileLoader, workspaceInstructions x2, workspaceMcpConfig) watching 8 kinds of config/workspace file. A subsystem port that first needs a layering decision (Rust engine vs TS host), not a default bump. Upstream hot-reloads; the fork only has explicit `/reload` and `/reload-tui`. **Docs half synced 2026-09-24** while the code half stays unported: `docs/{en,zh}/configuration/{config-files.md,env-vars.md}` taken byte-identical from `be7d5f5fea`, so the 2.1.1 changelog entry and the config reference do not contradict each other. Known resulting inaccuracy, recorded in ROADMAP §6.8.2: the fork documents `[watch] enabled` / `KIMI_CODE_WATCH` without implementing either (same class as `KIMI_CODE_SEARCH_WORKER` and `KIMI_CODE_PERSISTENCE_MINIDB_READMODEL`, both also verified absent here).

entries.subject: revert: roll back workspace trust-boundary hardening (#4013)
entries.note: **Followed (2026-09-24).** Reverts #3964, which this fork had ported (see §6.7). Upstream's stated reason is a product principle, not a defect: once a user trusts a repository, content inside it is the user's own responsibility, so the engine stops defending against it (PR #4013, `Root Cause: N/A`). Kept upstream and kept here: the fail-closed trust prompt and the lazy footer git detection — only the pre-trust window stays guarded. Removed in this fork, mirroring `929403b6db` line for line: (a) the static `-c` flags — `src/git.rs` deleted, its `CONFIG_ARGS`/`DIFF_ARGS` wiring removed from `tools/tower/git.rs` and `server/fs_routes.rs`; (b) the symlink re-resolution write gates — `native/path_access.rs::is_project_local_config_path`, `tools/mod.rs::symlink_lands_on_project_local_config` + both Write/Edit call sites, `permission/mod.rs` policy 12's opt-out; (c) the `local.toml` trust gate — `server/engine.rs::project_local_roots` no longer consults `is_workspace_trusted`; (d) the home / filesystem-root rejection in `project_local_config.rs` and `packages/node-sdk/src/project-local-config.ts`; (e) the TS side — `utils/git/git-args.ts` deleted, `utils/git/git-status.ts` + `feedback/codebase/scanner.ts` + `codebase-upload.test.ts` + `docs/{en,zh}/configuration/config-files.md` taken from `929403b6db` byte for byte. **Deliberately kept, because #4013 kept them too:** the whole `local.toml` read+write feature (post-revert v2 still calls `readAdditionalDirs` unconditionally and still renders `${additional_dirs_section}`) and `tools/mod.rs::resolve_for_write`'s canonicalization, which is `762f405811` (2026-08-30) baseline, not hardening. **Residual divergence:** `resolve_for_write` resolves write targets to their real path where post-revert v2 resolves lexically; observable only under the non-default `sandbox_write_guard`. Recorded in ROADMAP §6.8.1, not fixed this round.

entries.subject: feat: trust workspace via KIMI_CODE_TRUST_WORKSPACE env var (#4059)
entries.note: **Followed (2026-09-29).** `WorkspaceTrustService` gains an `envTrusted` flag read through `parseBooleanEnv` (`1/true/yes/on`), and `isTrusted()` returns `envTrusted || trusted` so the env outranks the persisted record. Implemented in the one place the fork keeps this state: `packages/node-sdk/src/native/sdk-rpc-client-native.ts::getWorkspaceTrustInfo` now short-circuits on the env before reading `trusted-workspaces.json`. `resolveSessionAdditionalDirs` needed no edit because it already routes through that accessor, which is what makes this a patch and not a feature. Tests: `packages/node-sdk/test/workspace-trust.test.ts` (5 cases: fail-closed, recorded trust, env outranks record, every truthy spelling, falsy or unrecognised spelling left alone). Documented in `docs/{en,zh}/configuration/env-vars.md`. Deliberately not ported: the `mcpRegistryService`/`workspaceMcpConfigService` hunks, because `gatedMcpServers` is hard-coded `[]` at `sdk-rpc-client-native.ts:5209` so there is no project-level MCP surface for trust to unlock; and the print-mode warning, whose string does not exist in this fork.

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): stop NotifyUser nudges in hosts without the update panel (#4054)
entries.note: v2 replaces the bare `NOTIFY_USER_FLAG_ID` check with `notifyUserAvailable(flagService, bootstrapService)` — a two-input gate: the flag AND a host that actually has an update panel. The fork has one input. `tools/mod.rs:1547` (the `notifyuser` / `notify_user` dispatch arm) validates only that the message is non-empty, then reports "Update shown to the user." unconditionally. The missing half is a host capability, not a case: the Rust engine has no notion of an update panel and `IBootstrapService` has no counterpart here. Porting means deciding where a host-side capability flag lives and who sets it, which is an interface decision rather than a patch.

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): publish permission mode changes on agent.status.updated (#4057)
entries.note: `permissionModeService` dispatches an `AgentStatusUpdated` carrying the new mode, and the event type gains an optional `permission` field. The fork has neither half: `src/events/types.rs` declares no `AgentStatus` / `agent_status` variant and no `permission` field on any event, so a permission-mode change has no wire representation at all. `injection/permission_mode.rs` is a turn-head reminder and is unrelated. This is a new event, not a missing case on an existing one, and it also needs a REST/WS contract decision: the fork owns those surfaces in `server/mod.rs` rather than in the TS layer v2 edits.

entries.subject: feat(tower): interrupt tower wake turns on user input and harden tower operations (#3998)
entries.note: Two separable halves, six independent clusters, plus one `n/a`. (a) Tower wake turns are interrupted on user input: v2 tracks the seeded turn through a `TurnStarted` subscription filtered on `origin.variant === tower_inbox` and cancels exactly that turn on `PromptSubmitted`, then re-arms the wake. The fork has no tower service, no injection-origin wake turn to identify, and no prompt-cancels-a-turn path at all — a prompt submitted during a turn is always steered in (`server/engine.rs:575` `enqueue_steer`). Nothing to extend. (b1) `TowerTeardown` gains live-agent protection, `exclude` and `dry_run`; the fork takes a bare `force` bool (`tools/tower/store.rs:1523`, schema at `mod.rs:1291`). (b2) death writes become session-guarded and activity-logged: `mark_agent_dead` (`store.rs:403`) takes one argument, writes no log line, and there is no revive path to guard. (b3) dead-by-intent versus died needs the death reason from (b2); `types.rs:31-39` carries `death_status` / `death_reason` for round-trip but nothing writes them. (b4) an inbox-before-completion gate needs `last_inbox_read_at`; the fork has `assert_completable` only (`store.rs:698`). (b5) a cross-process lockfile: the fork serialises `state.json` with a process-global mutex (`store.rs:28-43`), which cannot satisfy the two-OS-processes guarantee v2 added. **Not applicable:** v2 also renames the `state.json` tmp suffix to include pid+uuid, and the fork already writes per-writer tmp + atomic rename (`store.rs:295-307`) — same mechanism, different suffix, no observable change. Largest delta of the seven; every cluster is new surface.

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): remove interruption reminder on undo of its turn (#4076)
entries.note: Five lines in v2: `history.findLast(isUndoAnchor)?.id` becomes the reminder's `ownerPromptId`, so undoing the owning prompt takes the reminder with it. `isUndoAnchor` is `role === 'user'` plus an origin test — `inTurn !== true` and (no origin, or `kind === 'user'`, or (`skill_activation` / `plugin_command` with `trigger === 'user-slash'`)). The data the test needs is already carried: `LLMMessage` has both `origin: Option<Value>` (v2 `PromptOrigin`, set on the opening user message, `turn_loop/types.rs:189-196`) and `prompt_id: Option<String>` (`:188`). The gap is the consumer: the fork's undo is turn-based — `plan_undo_turns(session_id, count)` / `undo_turns` in `session/sqlite_store.rs:980,988` — and `grep prompt_id src/session/mod.rs` returns nothing, so nothing can ask which prompt a turn belongs to. Porting means adding prompt ownership to the undo path, which is a new concept rather than a missing case. `injection/interruption_reminder.rs` is unaware of undo today.

entries.subject: feat(kimi-code): summarize workspace trust with configuration sources (#4056)
entries.note: The untrusted-workspace prompt stops printing raw MCP commands and renders an activation summary instead: MCP servers that would start, folders outside the project, and instruction sources (AGENTS.md, skills, profiles), each with the config file it came from; paged with arrows and collapsed to a one-line prompt when the terminal is short. The fork has the prompt (`apps/kimi-code/src/tui/components/dialogs/trust-prompt.ts:46`) in its pre-commit shape and the trust bit, but nothing that composes "what trusting activates": `gatedMcpServers` is hard-coded `[]` (`sdk-rpc-client-native.ts:5209`, comment: "stays empty until the MCP catalog is wired"), `WorkspaceTrustInfo` has no `origin` / `gatedAdditionalDirs` / `additionalDirSources` / `warnings` / `instructionSources` (`node-sdk/src/types.ts:681-694`), and no project-origin MCP loader exists in the engine at all. The ingredients are all present separately (`project_local_config.rs:41-60` yields `config_path`, `prompt/agents_md.rs:71`, `skills/mod.rs:517`, `prompt/profiles.rs`) but unconnected. A disclosure service is a new module, so this is a feature.

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): fold UserPromptSubmit hook output into the prompt message (#4081)
entries.note: v2 stops making a hook's stdout a standalone `hook_result` user message and folds it into the prompt message as content parts at position 0, tagged `meta: { contentType, source: 'user prompt submit hook' }`, so one prompt always yields exactly one user message. The fork has neither producer nor marker: `tools/external_hooks.rs:273-288` `notify_user_prompt_submit` returns `()`, matches hooks and `spawn_hooks` (`:374-391`) discards every outcome — the comment at `:270-272` states the gap verbatim ("the engine currently only fires the observe path"). `ContentBlock` (`rpc/types.rs:487`) has no `meta` field, so there is nowhere to put the tag. `docs/{en,zh}/customization/hooks.md` claimed the blocking/append behaviour until 2026-09-29, when it was corrected to match. **Residual half-port found during triage:** the host layers still implement the pre-commit `hook_result` folding that no producer feeds — `packages/transcript/src/history/groupTurns.ts:482`, `foldFacts.ts:130`, `apps/kimi-code/src/tui/utils/message-replay.ts:332`, `session-replay.ts:215,274,338,365,651`, `node-sdk/src/types.ts:434`. The commit's companion skill-marking refactor (annotate-then-filter instead of `content.slice(bundled.length)`) is **not** a free refactor here: it needs `meta` on transcript content parts, which is the same contract change, so it travels with this entry rather than as a separate patch.

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): clear inherited cron tasks at the fork record (#4083)
entries.note: The mechanism it fixes does not exist here, and the fork has **two** cron surfaces — neither is session-scoped. v2 persists cron tasks as `cron.add` records in the session journal, so a fork — which copies that journal — inherited them and fired them from both sessions. In the fork: (1) **`fork_session` copies no state at all.** `session/sqlite_store.rs:834-861` does `load_session_history` -> `create_session_with_workspace` -> `UPDATE sessions SET parent_session_id` -> `save_turn(new_session_id, "turn-fork", 1, &history, None, None)`, with zero references to `state_entries` or `wire_events`. Both fork entry points go through it (`acp/mod.rs:1015`, `server/mod.rs:5130`), and the `btw` side channel does not fork a session at all — `napi_bindings.rs:3167-3170` seeds an in-memory subagent from `session.snapshot_history()`. (2) **The server-scoped surface is not per-session.** `server/mod.rs:595-599` documents entries under state key `("cron", "entries")`; `put_state` (`session/sqlite_store.rs:1336`) writes without a `session_id`, so the row stays NULL-owned and shared. (3) **The model-facing surface is not in the session store at all** — it is the workspace-keyed file store, `<home>/.kimi-code/engine-state/<workspace-key>/state/cron.json` (`storage/paths.rs:3-7`, `storage/state_store.rs:3-7`), keyed by a digest of the canonicalized workspace path. (4) **Session-scoped state exists but never holds cron.** `state_entries` does carry a `session_id` column (`session/sqlite_store.rs:516-530`) and `put_session_state` (`:1356`) sets it, but every caller uses it for `metadata` or `agent_config` only (`acp/mod.rs:475,526,684`; `server/mod.rs:1155,1183,5263,6001,7252,7259,7345,7352`) — never cron. So a fork shares the workspace's schedule exactly as every other session in that workspace does, which is the design rather than the bug, and the `cron_fork_cleared` reminder has no counterpart because telling the model "this fork has no scheduled tasks" would be false. The commit's other half (moving the `Forked` event class from `features/goal` to `session/agentLifecycle`, and widening `CronModelState` from a bare `Map` to `{ tasks, forkNotice }`) is v2 module layout with no Rust counterpart. **Verdict re-checked 2026-09-29 against a refreshed `.tmp/v2-ref-upstream` (`f409caa21e`)** after the first pass read only `cronService.ts` and missed surface (3).

entries.subject: feat: cap WaitFor at 90s and let new input end the wait (#4061)
entries.note: **Cap half ported 2026-09-29.** `WAIT_FOR_MAX_TIMEOUT_S` 600 -> 90 (`tools/task_tools.rs:28`), together with every site that stated the old bound: the `parse_timeout` doc comment, the `TASK_WAIT_DESCRIPTION` timeout guideline, the JSON-schema `maximum` and its description, the schema test, and `docs/{en,zh}/reference/tools.md`. Upstream decoupled the constant from `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_TIMEOUT_S` in this same commit (`export const WAIT_FOR_MAX_TIMEOUT_S = 90` replacing the alias); the fork's Bash background timeout stays 600, which upstream also left alone. The input schema is now **byte-identical** to upstream's `WaitForInputSchema` — both the `timeout` and the `task_id` description match character for character. **Not ported, and this is the larger half.** (a) The description prose: diffing the fork's `TASK_WAIT_DESCRIPTION` against upstream's `task-wait.md` shows 7 substantive differences beyond the number — upstream's opening is restrictive ("Only call this tool when you really have no other work to do") where the fork's is permissive, upstream adds "the user is kept waiting too" and a standalone "they notify you automatically" paragraph, adds a "think about what else you can do meanwhile" guideline and a "the result also lists other tasks that finished during the wait window" guideline, retightens the timeout guideline to "Prefer moving on to other work over calling WaitFor again", and drops the fork's steering guideline (upstream folded steering into the opening paragraph). (b) The per-turn repeat-wait tally and its `[wait_warning]` block with three advice variants (`taskWaitTool.ts` `countCall` / `withRepeatWarning` / `repeatWaitAdvice`). (c) The subagent-specific description (`task-wait-subagent.md`, appended when `scopeContext.agentId !== MAIN_AGENT_ID`) and the subagent-vs-main timeout wording. (d) The TUI half. **The fork's docs deliberately keep the `Ctrl-S`-only sentence** rather than upstream's "pressing `Enter` ... steers the message into the turn": steering here is gated on tower mode (`tui/controllers/message-dispatch.ts:652-666` `steerIntoCoordinator` requires `appState.towerMode`), so a plain Enter while the agent waits **queues** (`tui/commands/dispatch.ts:144-145` — "submissions through sendNormalUserInput queue while busy") and only `Ctrl-S` steers (`tui/controllers/editor-keyboard.ts:324` `onCtrlS`). Copying upstream's sentence would document behaviour this fork does not have.
